::: {.intro-panel .panel-ice .reveal}
## Research focus

My research interests lie at the intersection of **computational genomics, probabilistic modelling, sequence analysis, and machine learning**. I am especially interested in methods that preserve uncertainty in biological data instead of reducing complex evidence to a single deterministic answer.
:::

## Flagship project

::: {.research-feature .reveal}
<div class="eyebrow">CRISPR–CAS9 · PAIR HIDDEN MARKOV MODELS</div>

### Probabilistic modelling of CRISPR–Cas9 off-target interactions

CRISPR guide RNAs can interact with genomic sequences that differ from the intended target through **mismatches, insertions, or deletions**. Computational off-target analysis therefore depends not only on identifying similar sequences, but also on deciding how guide and target sequences should be aligned and interpreted.
:::

::: {.concept-panels .reveal}
::: {.concept-panel .panel-blue}
<div class="concept-number">01</div>
### Question
How can we represent uncertainty in guide–target alignment when prioritising possible CRISPR off-target sites?
:::

::: {.concept-panel .panel-teal}
<div class="concept-number">02</div>
### Approach
Use a **pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM)** with Match, Insertion, and Deletion states to represent guide–target relationships probabilistically.
:::

::: {.concept-panel .panel-sage}
<div class="concept-number">03</div>
### Key idea
Instead of relying only on one alignment path, probabilistic inference can retain support distributed across multiple plausible alignments.
:::

::: {.concept-panel .panel-ice}
<div class="concept-number">04</div>
### Application
Genome-wide candidate analysis and prioritisation for CRISPR–Cas9 off-target research.
:::
:::
